metadata.title: Ep 11, Best ITO Street Food Walk I Sardarji Paratha, Swadeshi Pizza, Moradabadi Dal, Udupi Spa Dosa
metadata.description:
ITO is a bustling hub of administration, commerce, and education in Delhi, recently became the backdrop for our food tour. Accompanied by our physician friend from MAMC, Akshat, we set out to explore the culinary gems of this vibrant neighborhood.  

We began at Yadav Nariyal Pani Bhandar, where we sipped on refreshing ripe coconut water. The young seller told us how the cart has been around for years, with the coconut pulp sold at traffic crossings while the water is served fresh here. It was the perfect start to our journey.  

At Hum Hindustani on Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, we stepped into what felt like a cosy co-working space where one could work while enjoying their favorite food. A true landmark of Ito’s culinary scene, we indulged in a posi dosa and chow chow bhaat. The flavors were bold, comforting, and deliciously authentic.  

On Vishnu Digamber Marg, we stopped for a Swadeshi Pizza for Moong Dal Pizza, essentially a moonglet with pizza toppings. The unique combination of textures and flavors made it a surprisingly delightful experience. We also sampled Muradabad dal here, a comforting yet zesty lentil based dish. 

Next, we tried a slightly different version of dabeli at the Bombay Special Food Stall near ESIC. The aalu masala inside was quite flavourful, setting this version apart from the usual.  

We ended our journey at Sardar Ji Parathe Wale near ITO Metro Gate No. 4. Run by a hardworking and genial Sardarji, the place offered freshly prepared parathas with a variety of curries. We opted for their anda paratha, a hearty creation combining aloo paratha with beaten egg stuffed inside. Watching it being made right in front of us was as enjoyable as eating it.  

This food tour through ITO gave us a taste of its vibrant culinary culture, blending traditional flavors with innovative twists.
